rows.subject: FaceMorph's own application code, scripts, tests, temporary root paths, fixtures/evidence JSON, HTML/SCSS, and the runtime modules and manifests it authored or generated
rows.licence: MIT (operator decision, 26 October 2026): the monorepo and the three npm packages. Classic itself declared none (no LICENSE/COPYING file at any classic commit; package.json "private": true with no license field)
rows.required_notice: The MIT copyright and permission notice: LICENSE at the repository root and in each npm package (stylegan-js, browser-model-manager, cloudflare-model-host), whose THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES list anything else they carry.
rows.restrictions: MIT: keep the copyright and permission notice with copies or substantial portions.
rows.provenance: check-face/facemorph.me-classic (repository id 295956585), candidate/next-delivery-20260916 at a42829bb0582b5a7a55ba6b1045a05861612b8a5. Commit authors in classic history are Chris Dilger and Oliver Coad (src/index.html and src/style.scss include commits by both). Runtime JS modules are byte-identical published copies of classic sources (photo-runtime/*.mjs, photo-runtime/encoder-stream/execute.mjs, src/Next/browser/fused-resample-v1.mjs); the published webgl-vector-v1.mjs (905abe6c...) is a frozen earlier build of src/Next/browser/webgl-vector-v1.mjs (now 6c680636...). photo-native.wasm/.mjs also contain FaceMorph's photo-runtime/native/photo.cpp and pillow_support.c. Manifests, sample-indices.i32, qualification reports and the grey no-face fixture are generated by FaceMorph's staging scripts.
evidence: classic a42829b: root tree (no LICENSE); `git log --all -- 'LICENSE*' 'COPYING*' 'license*'` returns nothing
classic a42829b: self-host/README.md ("No new license for the frontend is invented by this overlay")
classic a42829b: git log --format=%an over the allowlisted paths
rows.unresolved: The operator chose MIT on 26 October 2026, which this repository and its packages now carry. Still open: classic's history also has commits by Oliver Coad (src/index.html and src/style.scss), and nothing here records his agreement to MIT for those files. The NumPy RandomState reimplementation (src/Next/browser/identity.mjs, packages/stylegan-js/src/engine/identity.ts) has no record of whether it was translated from NumPy or mt19937ar.c, so stylegan-js's THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES reproduces both BSD notices. The legacy CheckFace backend's CC BY-NC 4.0 (self-host/licenses/CheckFace-LICENSE.txt) covers only that imported API source, not this code.

rows.subject: ONNX Runtime Web 1.24.3 CPU WASM: the threaded runtime (ort.wasm.min.mjs, ort-wasm-simd-threaded.mjs/.wasm) and the encoder stream's unshared serial runtime (ort-wasm-simd.mjs, ort-wasm-simd-256m.wasm)

Both are published at runtime notices/ONNX-Runtime-MIT.txt and notices/ONNX-Runtime-ThirdPartyNotices.txt (classic hosting/next/notices/ONNX-Runtime-ThirdPartyNotices.txt, byte-identical to experiment/device-lab/ort-unshared-1243-v1/ThirdPartyNotices.txt).
rows.provenance: Threaded build: onnxruntime-web 1.24.3 dist, copied by src/Next/browser/stage-assets.py from experiment/onnx/node_modules/onnxruntime-web/dist. Serial build: experiment/device-lab/ort-unshared-1243-v1, described in serial-factory-v1.js as the 'matching, unmodified ORT1.24.3 serial Emscripten factory', with ort-wasm-simd.wasm sha256 4b2d44a4... in ARTIFACTS.sha256 and LICENSE/ThirdPartyNotices kept beside it. photo-runtime/encoder-stream/stage.py changes only the WASM memory-section maximum (65,536 to 4,096 pages) to make ort-wasm-simd-256m.wasm (4381425d...) and copies ORT-LICENSE/ORT-ThirdPartyNotices into the stage. The mirrored runtime does not carry those two copies because the manifest does not pin them; the top-level notices/ copies cover the files. Nothing records where the unshared binary was built.

rows.subject: @ffmpeg/core 0.12.10 video codec fallback (ffmpeg-core.js and the chunked ffmpeg-core.wasm)
rows.licence: GNU General Public License v2.0 or later ("That core uses GPL-2.0-or-later", classic notices/index.html; npm registry license GPL-2.0-or-later)
rows.required_notice: GPL-2.0 sections 1 and 3: the licence text plus the complete corresponding source, or a written offer, for the exact build distributed. Classic ships only one paragraph linking the npm page and the upstream repository, with no GPL text.
rows.restrictions: Copyleft: redistribution of the binaries must preserve the GPL terms and make corresponding source available.
rows.provenance: Unmodified @ffmpeg/core 0.12.10 dist/esm (ffmpeg-core.js, ffmpeg-core.wasm) from experiment/device-lab/node_modules/@ffmpeg/core. Since restage-runtime.py --codec and prepare-runtime.py it is self-hosted and chunked on next.facemorph.me rather than fetched from cdn.jsdelivr.net.
evidence: PLAN.md (this repo): Known candidate defects #21 (notices page misstates where the video codec is served from)
rows.unresolved: The site now serves the GPL binaries itself, so FaceMorph is the distributor. notices/index.html still says they are fetched from the publisher's CDN (PLAN.md defect 21). Ship the GPL-2.0 text and either host the exact corresponding source (the @ffmpeg/core 0.12.10 tarball and the FFmpeg/library sources and build scripts it was built from) or include a written offer. A link to upstream build instructions alone may not satisfy section 3. The core's component libraries and their individual licences were not checked.

rows.subject: Everything derived from NVIDIA's StyleGAN2 FFHQ config-F generator: ONNX mapping and synthesis, average/noise buffers, WebGL coefficient tables and manifest, WebGPU prefix/suffix segments with split/metadata/filter/bias, the latent average inside the e4e encoder graph, and the generated canaries and images
rows.licence: Nvidia Source Code License-NC (StyleGAN2, Copyright (c) 2019 NVIDIA) for the config-F checkpoint, and the NVIDIA Source Code License for StyleGAN2 with Adaptive Discriminator Augmentation (ADA) (Copyright (c) 2021 NVIDIA) for the conversion and network code
rows.required_notice: Section 3.1: a complete copy of the licence with every distribution, with NVIDIA copyright and attribution notices kept unmodified. Classic publishes only the 2021 ADA text (runtime notices/NVIDIA-StyleGAN2-ADA.txt). The 2019 Nvidia Source Code License-NC that governs the checkpoint was kept only at classic experiment/hf/models/LEGACY_LICENSE.txt (byte-identical to NVlabs/stylegan2 LICENSE.txt); this repository publishes those bytes beside it as notices/NVIDIA-StyleGAN2-NC.txt (fm-qoc3).
rows.restrictions: Section 3.3: the Work and any derivative works may be used, or intended for use, only non-commercially, meaning for research or evaluation purposes only (NVIDIA excepted). Section 3.4: rights terminate on a patent claim. Section 3.5: no trademark rights.
rows.provenance: Official StyleGAN2 FFHQ config-F checkpoint stylegan2-ffhq-config-f.pkl (https://nvlabs-fi-cdn.nvidia.com/stylegan2/networks/stylegan2-ffhq-config-f.pkl in self-host/prepare_model.py), taken as a read-only copy of the deployed Triton server-api-1 checkpoint, source sha256 adf127ea7bb8a7788c8bdeda3c9937f7310b669b09ecf799ca53a631ff46948d (manifest modelSourceSha256). Converted with NVlabs/stylegan2-ada-pytorch legacy.py at d72cc7d041b42ec8e806021a205ed9349f87c6a4 (G_ema only, no retraining), then exported to ONNX (experiment/onnx), WebGL vector16 coefficients and WebGPU mobile-fusion segments. The e4e encoder ONNX keeps the latent average ('Preserved in original final graph nodes'). The runtime manifest's distribution.purpose is 'research-and-evaluation', and notices/index.html says 'This candidate is for non-commercial research and evaluation. The model terms apply to the converted ONNX and GPU coefficient bundles as well.'
evidence: classic a42829b: experiment/hf/vendor/stylegan2-ada-pytorch/LICENSE.txt (same bytes as the shipped ADA notice)
classic a42829b: experiment/onnx/e4e_export.py (latent_avg added to the exported encoder)
rows.unresolved: (1) Is serving the converted weights to every visitor of next.facemorph.me, and later facemorph.me, 'research or evaluation' use under section 3.3? Any commercial or general public operation needs NVIDIA's permission. (2) Are generated images and latents 'derivative works' bound by section 3.3?

rows.subject: Flickr-Faces-HQ (FFHQ) training data behind both the StyleGAN2 config-F generator and the e4e FFHQ encoder, as it bears on their weights and outputs
rows.licence: The FFHQ dataset itself is Creative Commons BY-NC-SA 4.0 (NVIDIA). Individual images are CC BY 2.0, CC BY-NC 2.0, Public Domain Mark 1.0, CC0 1.0 or U.S. Government Works.
rows.required_notice: If the weights or outputs count as adaptations: credit by citing the FFHQ paper, indicate changes, and distribute derivatives under the same licence. Classic's web notices never mention FFHQ. Only the retired native NOTICE (desktop/scripts/stage-native-notices.py) linked https://github.com/NVlabs/ffhq-dataset#licenses. This repository publishes the dataset's licence statement as notices/FFHQ-terms.txt (fm-qoc3).
rows.restrictions: Non-commercial only (dataset CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and the BY-NC image licences). ShareAlike for derivatives of the dataset.
rows.provenance: src/explain.md: 'The model was trained on the Flickr-Faces-HQ dataset'. The e4e upstream README lists the checkpoint as 'FFHQ Inversion — FFHQ e4e encoder'. Neither the weights nor the images are a copy of the dataset.
rows.unresolved: Are trained weights and generated faces adaptations of the FFHQ dataset (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) or of individual Flickr images? If so, NonCommercial, ShareAlike and attribution reach the published runtime and any npm/model hosting. notices/FFHQ-terms.txt (fm-qoc3) quotes the dataset's terms; it does not settle the question.

rows.subject: encoder4editing (e4e) source code: the encoder architecture the ONNX graph was exported from, and the FFHQ alignment geometry ported into photo-native.wasm
rows.required_notice: The e4e MIT copyright and permission notice (runtime notices/e4e-MIT.txt). It is not repeated in photo/<hash>/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt, although photo-native.wasm contains the alignment port.
rows.provenance: omertov/encoder4editing, via the deployed olicoad/encoder4editing container copied on 11 September 2026 (self-host/e4e/PROVENANCE.md). The ONNX graph was exported by experiment/onnx/e4e_export.py from the e4e Encoder. photo-runtime/native/photo.cpp is the 'Original dlib20.0.1 detector/predictor and e4e alignment geometry' (README: 'original e4e alignment geometry').

rows.subject: Pretrained e4e FFHQ encoder weights: the monolithic encoder.onnx (64 chunks), its 108 streamed shards, and the W+ latents it produced for canaries
rows.licence: No licence stated for the pretrained checkpoint (the upstream repository is MIT, and its README states no separate model terms)
rows.required_notice: None established. Ship the e4e MIT notice and the NVIDIA and FFHQ terms that may reach the weights.
rows.restrictions: Inherited and unsettled: training data is FFHQ (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Per the e4e README, each e4e model 'contains the entire pSp framework architecture, including the encoder and decoder weights', and the decoder is the rosinality port of NVIDIA's FFHQ StyleGAN2. The exported graph keeps that decoder's latent average.
rows.provenance: e4e_ffhq_encode.pt, 1,201,649,680 bytes, sha256 2ace1d9a8c05c10a399bcd500b8dda118f759ff1aac89dbdab7435f2136a0999, from Google Drive id 1cUv_reLE6k3604or78EranS7XzuVMWeO as linked from https://github.com/omertov/encoder4editing#pretrained-models (self-host/encoder_assets.py). Exported by experiment/onnx/e4e_export.py to a 256px-to-W+ ONNX with latent_avg added (encoder.onnx d525a985..., 1,068,862,265 bytes), then split unchanged into 108 sequential shards by photo-runtime/encoder-stream/export.py.
evidence: classic a42829b: self-host/e4e/PROVENANCE.md ('Code's MIT license does not override model/data terms')
rows.unresolved: Upstream states no licence for the weights, so no redistribution grant is recorded. The checkpoint and the exported graph also carry StyleGAN2 decoder material (latent average) derived from NVIDIA's non-commercial model and were trained on FFHQ. Serving the 1 GB encoder publicly, or hosting it for package users, is not established as permitted.

rows.subject: dlib 68-point face landmark predictor shape_predictor_68_face_landmarks.dat (served in six chunks and streamed into photo-native.wasm)
rows.licence: No licence stated for the model file. dlib's notice: 'the license for the iBUG 300-W dataset excludes commercial use'
rows.required_notice: State the iBUG 300-W non-commercial restriction and point to the upstream predictor notice. Classic notices/index.html does both and links https://www.dlib.net/face_landmark_detection_ex.cpp.html.
rows.restrictions: Trained on iBUG 300-W, whose licence excludes commercial use. Upstream: 'you should contact Imperial College London to find out if it's OK for you to use this model file in a commercial product'.
rows.provenance: https://dlib.net/files/shape_predictor_68_face_landmarks.dat.bz2, decompressed to 99,693,937 bytes, sha256 fbdc2cb80eb9aa7a758672cbfdda32ba6300efe9b6e6c7a299ff7e736b11b92f (self-host/encoder_assets.py, photo-runtime/make-fixtures.py). dlib implementation of Kazemi and Sullivan (CVPR 2014), trained on iBUG 300-W (Sagonas et al., IMAVIS 2016).
rows.unresolved: Neither dlib nor classic addresses redistribution of the model file itself, which next.facemorph.me re-serves in six chunks. The 300-W terms exclude commercial use, and any commercial use needs Imperial College London's permission.
